title: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust acquires majority stake in AWS joint venture for $5bn
html:
Blackstone’s new publicly traded data center real estate investment trust (REIT) will acquire a majority interest in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services (AWS).

In its first investment, Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC) will take a 75 percent stake in the joint ventures, which, combined, will own 13 newly constructed powered shells across two AWS data center campuses.

The transaction is valued at around $5 billion, with an initial capitalization rate of seven percent, which puts Blackstone’s yearly net operating income for the investment at around $350 million.

AWS will retain the remaining 25 percent stake and lease back the entire portfolio on a triple net basis, meaning it will pay taxes, insurance, and maintenance on the properties. The initial lease term will be for 12 years, with a fully extended lease term of 32 years.

Specific details about the campuses were not disclosed.

“We are thrilled to announce BXDC’s inaugural investment and our partnership with Amazon, a leading global technology company with a long-term commitment to innovation,” said Nick Pell, CEO and president of BXDC. “The quality, basis, and tenant profile of these assets make this an attractive match for the deployment of our IPO proceeds. Given the deep expertise across our platform, we believe BXDC is well positioned to capitalize on a highly compelling opportunity and deliver value for our shareholders.”

Prasad Kalyanaraman, VP of AWS Infrastructure, added: "As we scale to meet growing demand for our customers, we're committed to building in a way that strengthens the communities where we operate.

“We're focused on delivering long-term local benefits, from creating good jobs and free workforce training programs to supporting local priorities. Partnering with Blackstone allows us to continue expanding responsibly while keeping communities at the center of how we build.”

Blackstone said it expects the transaction to close in Q4 2026, subject to conditions.

Blackstone took BXDC public in May this year, with plans to invest in newly constructed data center assets leased to hyperscale tenants on long-term contracts. The company said it would focus mainly on Tier 1 markets in North America.

BXDC raised about $1.75 billion in gross proceeds from its initial public offering (IPO) at $20 per share. The company’s share price remained relatively flat in its first few months before slipping in late September and hovering around $15 in October.

Shares in BXDC rose six percent today following the announcement, reaching almost $18 per share, though still below the IPO price.

Blackstone has been a major investor in data centers, with more than $130bn invested since 2018 and more than $10bn in debt financing provided to data center and digital infrastructure developers and operators.

The alternative asset manager owns data center developers QTS and AirTrunk, and has stakes in many other companies across the market.
summary: The publicly traded REIT’s inaugural deal covers 13 newly constructed powered shells
